claim: Osteoblast dedifferentiation is characterized by downregulation of bone gamma-carboxyglutamic acid-containing protein (bglap) at 12 hours post-amputation (hpa).
source: This process is characterized by the downregulation of mature markers, such as bone gamma-carboxyglutamic acid-containing protein (bglap) at 12 hpa (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Long, 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Long, 2011) that established this finding.

claim: Osteoblast dedifferentiation is characterized by upregulation of the pre-osteoblast marker runx2 at 24 hpa.
source: This process is characterized by the downregulation of mature markers, such as bone gamma-carboxyglutamic acid-containing protein (bglap) at 12 hpa (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Long, 2011), and upregulation of the pre-OB marker, runx2, at 24 hpa (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Salhotra et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Salhotra et al., 2020).

claim: Osteoblasts undergoing dedifferentiation detach from the bony-ray surface via an EMT-like event.
source: OBs undergoing dedifferentiation detach from the bony-ray surface via an EMT-like event, migrate toward the stump region, re-enter the cell cycle and form a pool of pre-OB cells that incorporates the blastema (Figure 1A; Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Stewart et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Stewart et al., 2014) and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Osteoblasts undergoing dedifferentiation migrate toward the stump region.
source: OBs undergoing dedifferentiation detach from the bony-ray surface via an EMT-like event, migrate toward the stump region, re-enter the cell cycle and form a pool of pre-OB cells that incorporates the blastema (Figure 1A; Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Stewart et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Stewart et al., 2014) and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Osteoblasts undergoing dedifferentiation re-enter the cell cycle.
source: OBs undergoing dedifferentiation detach from the bony-ray surface via an EMT-like event, migrate toward the stump region, re-enter the cell cycle and form a pool of pre-OB cells that incorporates the blastema (Figure 1A; Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Stewart et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Stewart et al., 2014) and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Osteoblasts undergoing dedifferentiation form a pool of pre-osteoblast cells that incorporates the blastema.
source: OBs undergoing dedifferentiation detach from the bony-ray surface via an EMT-like event, migrate toward the stump region, re-enter the cell cycle and form a pool of pre-OB cells that incorporates the blastema (Figure 1A; Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Stewart et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011; Stewart et al., 2014) and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: At 6 hpa, bglap is downregulated in regenerating caudal fins relative to uninjured caudal fins (0 hpa).
source: We observed a downregulation of bglap and upregulation of runx2a (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, which displays relative gene expression at 6 hpa compared to 0 hpa.

claim: At 6 hpa, runx2a is upregulated in regenerating caudal fins relative to uninjured caudal fins (0 hpa).
source: We observed a downregulation of bglap and upregulation of runx2a (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, which displays relative gene expression at 6 hpa compared to 0 hpa.

claim: Mature osteoblasts are already undergoing transcriptional changes consistent with dedifferentiation as early as 6 hpa.
source: We observed a downregulation of bglap and upregulation of runx2a (Figure 1B) suggesting that, in contrast to previous studies (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011), mature OBs are already undergoing transcriptional changes consistent with dedifferentiation as early as 6 hpa.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data (Figure 1B) showing gene expression changes at 6 hpa, and contrasts with previous studies (Knopf et al., 2011; Sousa et al., 2011).

claim: Osteoblasts from the segment below amputation (segment 0) become motile at the 5-10 hpa time-interval.
source: Tracking of bglap-positive (Bglap+) OBs revealed that OBs from the segment below amputation (segment 0) become motile at the 5–10 hpa time-interval and in average reach the amputation plane around 20–25 hpa (Figure 1C and D)
evidence: The claim is supported by live-imaging data tracking osteoblast movement shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Osteoblasts from segment 0 reach the amputation plane on average around 20-25 hpa.
source: Tracking of bglap-positive (Bglap+) OBs revealed that OBs from the segment below amputation (segment 0) become motile at the 5–10 hpa time-interval and in average reach the amputation plane around 20–25 hpa (Figure 1C and D)
evidence: The claim is supported by live-imaging data tracking osteoblast movement shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Bglap-positive osteoblasts from the second segment (segment-1) remain predominantly immotile.
source: Tracking of bglap-positive (Bglap+) OBs revealed that OBs from the segment below amputation (segment 0) become motile at the 5–10 hpa time-interval and in average reach the amputation plane around 20–25 hpa (Figure 1C and D), while Bglap +OB from the second segment (segment-1) remain predominantly immotile (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The proportion of Bglap-positive osteoblasts entering the cell cycle progressively increases from 12 to 24 hpa.
source: Immunofluorescence for PCNA (marker of G1 phase) indicated that the proportion of Bglap +OBs entering the cell cycle progressively increases, specifically from 12 to 24 hpa (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for PCNA shown in Figure 1E.

claim: At 24 hpa, almost 80% of Bglap-positive osteoblasts in the first segment have entered the G1 phase.
source: At 24 hpa, almost 80% of Bglap +OBs in the first segment have entered the G1 phase (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: At 0 hpa (homeostasis), Runx2 is observed in the nucleus of bone-lining mature osteoblasts.
source: In homeostasis conditions (0 hpa), Runx2 is observed in the nucleus of bone-lining mature OB (Runx2 +Bglap + ; Figure 1F, F' and H)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1F, F' and H.

claim: Runx2 is expressed at basal levels in fully differentiated osteoblasts.
source: In homeostasis conditions (0 hpa), Runx2 is observed in the nucleus of bone-lining mature OB (Runx2 +Bglap + ; Figure 1F, F' and H), which is in accordance with Runx2 being expressed at basal levels in fully differentiated OB (Conaway et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Conaway et al., 2013) and is consistent with the observed data.

claim: At 12 and 24 hpa, there is a slight decrease in the total number of Runx2+Bglap+ osteoblasts within the first segment below amputation.
source: At 12 and 24 hpa, we observed a slight decrease in the total number of Runx2 +Bglap + OB population within the first segment below amputation (Figure 1G, G' and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 1G, G' and H.

claim: Osteoblasts are not described to undergo apoptosis at 12 and 24 hpa.
source: OBs are not described to undergo apoptosis at this stage (Knopf et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Knopf et al., 2011).

claim: The decrease in Runx2+Bglap+ osteoblasts could be due to loss of the bglap differentiation marker in a portion of dedifferentiated osteoblasts.
source: OBs are not described to undergo apoptosis at this stage (Knopf et al., 2011), suggesting that decrease in the Runx2 +Bglap + OBs could be due to actual loss of the bglap differentiation marker in a portion of dedifferentiated OB.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that osteoblasts do not undergo apoptosis (Knopf et al., 2011), combined with the observed decrease in Runx2+Bglap+ cells.

claim: Remaining Runx2+Bglap+ osteoblasts possess higher levels of Runx2 at 12 and 24 hpa compared to 0 hpa.
source: Nevertheless, remaining Runx2 +Bglap + possess higher levels of Runx2 when compared to Runx2 +Bglap + OBs at 0 hpa (Figure 1F–G' arrows)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1F-G'.

claim: Remaining Runx2+Bglap+ osteoblasts converted into a pre-osteoblast phenotype.
source: Nevertheless, remaining Runx2 +Bglap + possess higher levels of Runx2 when compared to Runx2 +Bglap + OBs at 0 hpa (Figure 1F–G' arrows), further indicating that they converted into a pre-OB phenotype, in accordance with published data (Mishra et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data (Figure 1F-G') and citation to a previous study (Mishra et al., 2020).

claim: At 0 hpa, a small number of pre-osteoblasts (Runx2+Bglap-) was detected in the bony-rays intersegment/joint.
source: In addition, at 0 hpa a small number of pre-OB (Runx2 +Bglap-) was detected in the bony-rays intersegment/joint (Figure 1F and F' asterisk,I)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1F, F' and I.

claim: The Runx2+Bglap- cells detected at the intersegment/joint at 0 hpa may correspond to a population of osteoblast progenitors referred as joint OP.
source: In addition, at 0 hpa a small number of pre-OB (Runx2 +Bglap-) was detected in the bony-rays intersegment/joint (Figure 1F and F' asterisk,I), which may correspond to a population of OB progenitors (OPs) recently identified in this region, refered as joint OP (Ando et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data (Figure 1F, F' and I) and citation to a previous study (Ando et al., 2017).

claim: At 12 and 24 hpa, there is an increase in the number of Runx2+Bglap- cells.
source: At 12 and 24 hpa, we observed an increase in the number of Runx2 +Bglap cells, suggesting that pre-OB arise in the first 12 hpa and their numbers increase until the beginning of blastema formation at 24 hpa (Figure 1F-G' and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 1F-G' and I.

claim: Pre-osteoblasts arise in the first 12 hpa and their numbers increase until the beginning of blastema formation at 24 hpa.
source: At 12 and 24 hpa, we observed an increase in the number of Runx2 +Bglap cells, suggesting that pre-OB arise in the first 12 hpa and their numbers increase until the beginning of blastema formation at 24 hpa (Figure 1F-G' and I).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed increase in Runx2+Bglap- cells shown in Figure 1F-G' and I.

claim: Mature osteoblasts lose their differentiated character and contribute to the pre-osteoblast pool in a time-window between 12 and 24 hpa.
source: Altogether, these data indicate that mature OBs lose their differentiated character and contribute to the pre-OB pool in a time-window between 12 and 24 hpa.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined experimental data presented in the section.

claim: Pre-osteoblasts can also arise from the joint-associated osteoblast progenitor niche.
source: Nevertheless, we cannot exclude that pre-OB can also arise from the joint-associated OB progenitor niche.
evidence: The claim is speculative, acknowledging an alternative source of pre-osteoblasts.

claim: At 24 hpa, multiple osteoblast sources are recruited to contribute to the blastema.
source: Thus, we hypothesize that at 24 hpa, multiple OB sources are recruited to contribute to the blastema (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on the data presented and illustrated in Figure 1J.

claim: Mature osteoblast dedifferentiation is an early response to injury.
source: Here, we show that mature OB dedifferentiation is an early response to injury and entails important transcriptional and phenotypic alterations, occurring in a narrow time-window between 6–12 hpa, before blastema induction and during the wound healing phase.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

source: Here, we show that mature OB dedifferentiation is an early response to injury and entails important transcriptional and phenotypic alterations, occurring in a narrow time-window between 6–12 hpa, before blastema induction and during the wound healing phase.

claim: Osteoblasts were isolated by FACS using the bglap:EGFP transgenic line.
source: OBs were isolated by FACS using the bglap:EGFP transgenic line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental method used, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Osteoblasts show a dynamic transcriptional response at 6 hpa in comparison to osteoblasts from uninjured conditions with almost 2200 differentially expressed genes.
source: We observed that OBs show a dynamic transcriptional response at 6 hpa in comparison to OBs from uninjured conditions with almost 2200 differentially expressed genes, from which 1040 were downregulated and 1130 were upregulated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: At 6 hpa, 1040 genes were downregulated in osteoblasts compared to uninjured conditions.
source: We observed that OBs show a dynamic transcriptional response at 6 hpa in comparison to OBs from uninjured conditions with almost 2200 differentially expressed genes, from which 1040 were downregulated and 1130 were upregulated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: At 6 hpa, 1130 genes were upregulated in osteoblasts compared to uninjured conditions.
source: We observed that OBs show a dynamic transcriptional response at 6 hpa in comparison to OBs from uninjured conditions with almost 2200 differentially expressed genes, from which 1040 were downregulated and 1130 were upregulated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The dedifferentiation machinery is triggered very early during regeneration.
source: These data further demonstrates that the dedifferentiation machinery is triggered very early during regeneration
evidence: The claim is inferred from the transcriptomic data showing extensive gene expression changes at 6 hpa.

claim: A large set of genes related to energy metabolism was dramatically altered at 6 hpa in osteoblasts.
source: Importantly, a large set of genes related to energy metabolism was also dramatically altered (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data provided in Supplementary file 1.

claim: At 6 hpa, osteoblasts upregulate the expression of major glycolytic enzymes such as hexokinase 1 (hk1) and phosphofructokinase (pfkp).
source: From our transcriptome data set of DE, we observed that at 6 hpa OBs upregulate the expression of major glycolytic enzymes, such as hexokinase 1 (hk1) and phosphofructokinase (pfkp), whereas OXPHOS components remain mostly unchanged (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: At 6 hpa, OXPHOS components in osteoblasts remain mostly unchanged.
source: From our transcriptome data set of DE, we observed that at 6 hpa OBs upregulate the expression of major glycolytic enzymes, such as hexokinase 1 (hk1) and phosphofructokinase (pfkp), whereas OXPHOS components remain mostly unchanged (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: At 6 hpa, there is a significant increase in lactate dehydrogenase (ldha) expression in osteoblasts.
source: Most importantly, we detected a significant increase in lactate dehydrogenase (ldha) expression, suggesting an increase in lactate production, possibly by diverting pyruvate from mitochondrial oxidation. (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The increase in ldha expression suggests an increase in lactate production, possibly by diverting pyruvate from mitochondrial oxidation.
source: Most importantly, we detected a significant increase in lactate dehydrogenase (ldha) expression, suggesting an increase in lactate production, possibly by diverting pyruvate from mitochondrial oxidation. (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed increase in ldha expression shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Dedifferentiating osteoblasts change their metabolic signature, adopting a metabolic program that increases glycolysis.
source: These data suggest that dedifferentiating OBs change their metabolic signature, adopting a metabolic program that increases glycolysis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the transcriptomic data showing upregulation of glycolytic enzymes and ldha.

claim: Osteoblasts account for around 1-3% of the total cell number in a bony-ray segment.
source: Since OBs only account for around 1–3% of the total cell number in a bony-ray segment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: At 6 hpa, most glycolytic enzymes were highly upregulated in the whole fin stump, including hk1, hk2, pfkpa, and pyruvate kinase (pkma).
source: At 6 hpa, when cells start to dedifferentiate, most glycolytic enzymes were highly upregulated, including hk1, hk2, pfkpa, and pyruvate kinase (pkma) (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: At 6 hpa, ldha expression was increased in the whole fin stump.
source: Importantly, as observed during OB dedifferentiation, ldha expression was increased and pyruvate dehydrogenase a 1b (pdha1b) was downregulated.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: At 6 hpa, pyruvate dehydrogenase a 1b (pdha1b) was downregulated in the whole fin stump.
source: Importantly, as observed during OB dedifferentiation, ldha expression was increased and pyruvate dehydrogenase a 1b (pdha1b) was downregulated.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Pdha1b is part of the Pdh1 complex, which catalyzes irreversibly the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA.
source: pdha1b is part of the Pdh1 complex, which catalyzes irreversibly the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA and progression to OXPHOS
evidence: The claim is based on established biochemical knowledge about the Pdh1 complex.

claim: The downregulation of pdha1b corroborates that at 6 hpa pyruvate is being shunt from the mitochondria and stimulating lactate-producing glycolysis.
source: pdha1b is part of the Pdh1 complex, which catalyzes irreversibly the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA and progression to OXPHOS, further corroborating that at this stage pyruvate is being shunt from the mitochondria and stimulating lactate-producing glycolysis (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed downregulation of pdha1b shown in Figure 2C, combined with knowledge of its biochemical function.

claim: At 6 hpa, most OXPHOS components analyzed remained unchanged or slightly upregulated in the whole fin stump.
source: As for the OXPHOS components analyzed, most remained unchanged or slightly upregulated. However, this increase in expression was not as accentuated as the one observed for the glycolytic pathway (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: At 24 hpa, most glycolytic enzymes were still significantly upregulated in the whole fin stump, although not as striking as at 6 hpa.
source: Later, at 24 hpa, when most cells have dedifferentiated and the blastema starts to be assembled, we observed that most glycolytic enzymes were still significantly upregulated, although not as striking as at 6 hpa time-point, and ldha expression continued to be upregulated (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: At 24 hpa, ldha expression continued to be upregulated in the whole fin stump.
source: Later, at 24 hpa, when most cells have dedifferentiated and the blastema starts to be assembled, we observed that most glycolytic enzymes were still significantly upregulated, although not as striking as at 6 hpa time-point, and ldha expression continued to be upregulated (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: At 24 hpa, there is an increase in expression of some OXPHOS components in the whole fin stump.
source: At this time-point, we also observed an increase in expression of some OXPHOS components (Figure 2D), suggesting that blastema formation may also require mitochondrial glucose oxidation.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Blastema formation may also require mitochondrial glucose oxidation.
source: At this time-point, we also observed an increase in expression of some OXPHOS components (Figure 2D), suggesting that blastema formation may also require mitochondrial glucose oxidation.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the observed increase in OXPHOS component expression at 24 hpa shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Consistent upregulation of genes associated with glycolysis and lactate production suggests that the osteoblast dedifferentiation process and possibly the early response to amputation are characterized by a metabolic adaptation toward glycolysis.
source: Consistent upregulation of the genes associated with glycolysis and lactate production suggests that the OB dedifferentiation process and possibly the early response to amputation are characterized by a metabolic adaptation toward glycolysis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the consistent upregulation of glycolytic genes observed in the data.

claim: There is an increase in glucose at 6 and 24 hpa in relation to control fins (0 hpa).
source: According with our transcriptome data, we observed an increase in glucose and lactate at 6 and 24 hpa in relation to control fins (0 hpa), which is consistent with an increment in the glycolytic influx (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: There is an increase in lactate at 6 and 24 hpa in relation to control fins (0 hpa).
source: According with our transcriptome data, we observed an increase in glucose and lactate at 6 and 24 hpa in relation to control fins (0 hpa), which is consistent with an increment in the glycolytic influx (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The increase in glucose and lactate at 6 and 24 hpa is consistent with an increment in the glycolytic influx.
source: According with our transcriptome data, we observed an increase in glucose and lactate at 6 and 24 hpa in relation to control fins (0 hpa), which is consistent with an increment in the glycolytic influx (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the metabolite measurements shown in Figure 2E, combined with the transcriptome data.

claim: There is a strong increase of glutamine and glutamate at 24 hpa but not at 6 hpa.
source: We also observed a strong increase of glutamine and glutamate at 24 hpa but not at 6 hpa (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Glutamine and glutamate act as important substrates for protein and nucleotide synthesis necessary to support cellular integrity and growth.
source: Glutamine and glutamate act as important substrates for protein and nucleotide synthesis necessary to support cellular integrity and growth suggesting an increase in biosynthesis (Newsholme et al., 2003; Yoo et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Newsholme et al., 2003; Yoo et al., 2020).

claim: The increase in glutamine and glutamate at 24 hpa suggests an increase in biosynthesis.
source: Glutamine and glutamate act as important substrates for protein and nucleotide synthesis necessary to support cellular integrity and growth suggesting an increase in biosynthesis (Newsholme et al., 2003; Yoo et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed increase in glutamine and glutamate at 24 hpa, combined with knowledge of their biochemical roles (Newsholme et al., 2003; Yoo et al., 2020).

claim: In control fins (0 hpa), glucose uptake is detected in the intersegment region.
source: In control fins (0 hpa), we detected glucose uptake in the intersegment region (Figure 2F–H arrows,L,N)
evidence: The claim is supported by 2-NBDG uptake imaging data shown in Figure 2F-H, L, N.

claim: A population of osteoblast progenitors have been identified in the intersegment region.
source: In control fins (0 hpa), we detected glucose uptake in the intersegment region (Figure 2F–H arrows,L,N), where a population of OP have been identified (Ando et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Ando et al., 2017).

claim: Under homeostatic conditions, osteoblast progenitor cells in the intersegment region may require higher levels of glucose to maintain the progenitor niche.
source: In control fins (0 hpa), we detected glucose uptake in the intersegment region (Figure 2F–H arrows,L,N), where a population of OP have been identified (Ando et al., 2017), which may imply that under homeostatic conditions, these cells require higher levels of glucose to maintain the progenitor niche.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the observed glucose uptake in the intersegment region shown in Figure 2F-H, L, N, combined with knowledge of the OP population (Ando et al., 2017).

claim: At 24 hpa, there is a significant increase of glucose uptake in the blastema primordium and in the first segment below the amputation.
source: At 24 hpa, we observed a significant increase of glucose uptake in the blastema primordium and in the first segment below the amputation (Figure 2I–K, M and N).
evidence: The claim is supported by 2-NBDG uptake imaging data shown in Figure 2I-K, M and N.

claim: There is an increase in expression of genes associated with mitochondrial fission, namely drp1 and fis1, at 6 hpa but not at 24 hpa, when compared to uninjured condition (0 hpa).
source: By performing a qPCR analysis at 0, 6, and 24 hpa, we observed an increase in expression of genes associated with mitochondrial fission, namely drp1 and fis1, at 6 hpa but not at 24 hpa, when compared to uninjured condition (0 hpa) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: There is an increase in the number of mitochondria per cell at 6 and 24 hpa, in relation to uninjured control.
source: By quantifying the number of mitochondria using the reporter line MLS-GFP, which labels the mitochondria membrane (Kim et al., 2008), we noticed an increase in the number of mitochondria per cell at 6 and 24 hpa, in relation to uninjured control (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-H',I).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of mitochondria using the MLS-GFP reporter line shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-H',I.

claim: There is a significant increase in percentage of mitochondria smaller than 0.1 µm³ at 6 hpa.
source: In accordance with an increase in mitochondria fission, we observed a significant increase in percentage of mitochondria smaller than 0,1 µm3 at 6 hpa, while at 24 hpa the mitochondria size profile is similar to the 0 hpa condition (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-H',J).
evidence: The claim is supported by mitochondria volume measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-H',J.

claim: At 24 hpa, the mitochondria size profile is similar to the 0 hpa condition.
source: In accordance with an increase in mitochondria fission, we observed a significant increase in percentage of mitochondria smaller than 0,1 µm3 at 6 hpa, while at 24 hpa the mitochondria size profile is similar to the 0 hpa condition (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-H',J).
evidence: The claim is supported by mitochondria volume measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-H',J.

claim: The early stages of regeneration involve an upregulation of glycolytic activity, which is accompanied by a temporally restricted program of mitochondria fission.
source: Taken together, these results are in consistent with an increase in mitochondrial fission triggered by amputation and further supports the hypothesis that the early stages of regeneration involve an upregulation of glycolytic activity, which is accompanied by a temporally restricted program of mitochondria fission.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined data on glycolytic gene expression, metabolite levels, and mitochondrial fission.

claim: Metabolic adaptation enhancing glycolysis seems to constitute an integral response to amputation, tightly regulated in terms of time and space.
source: Thus, metabolic adaptation enhancing glycolysis seems to constitute an integral response to amputation, tightly regulated in terms of time and space.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

claim: Cells respond to injury by increasing the glycolytic influx, lactate production and mitochondrial fission just preceding dedifferentiation and blastema formation.
source: Our transcriptome and metabolome studies indicate a specific metabolic signature as part of an early response to amputation by OBs and by the remaining caudal fin tissue. Overall, cells respond to injury by increasing the glycolytic influx, lactate production and mitochondrial fission just preceding dedifferentiation and blastema formation.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the transcriptome and metabolome data presented in the section.

claim: Amputation induces a reprogramming of the metabolic profile.
source: These results corroborate the hypothesis that amputation induces a reprogramming of the metabolic profile, which may be part of a general program that coordinates the regenerative response.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

claim: The blastema is a hallmark and prerequisite of epimorphic regeneration.
source: The blastema is a hallmark and prerequisite of epimorphic regeneration and is fully assembled within 48 hpa (Kawakami, 2010; Poss et al., 2003; Pfefferli and Jaźwińska, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Kawakami, 2010; Poss et al., 2003; Pfefferli and Jaźwińska, 2015).

claim: The blastema is fully assembled within 48 hpa.
source: The blastema is a hallmark and prerequisite of epimorphic regeneration and is fully assembled within 48 hpa (Kawakami, 2010; Poss et al., 2003; Pfefferli and Jaźwińska, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Kawakami, 2010; Poss et al., 2003; Pfefferli and Jaźwińska, 2015).

claim: 2-Deoxy-D-glucose (2DG) competes with glucose for hexokinase catalytic domain, inhibiting the downstream products derived from glucose.
source: Firstly, we inhibited glycolysis using an established glucose analogue, 2-Deoxy-D-glucose (2DG) (Sinclair et al., 2021; Honkoop et al., 2019), that competes with glucose for Hk catalytic domain, the first step of glycolysis, inhibiting the downstream products derived from glucose.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Sinclair et al., 2021; Honkoop et al., 2019) and describes the mechanism of action of 2DG.

claim: The higher the duration of 2DG treatment, the stronger the effect on blastema growth in comparison to control fins.
source: We observed that the higher the duration of the treatment the stronger the effect on blastema growth in comparison to control fins (Figure 3C and D–K).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of regenerated area shown in Figure 3C and D-K.

claim: A single dose of 2DG administered at 0 hpa showed significant smaller regenerates when compared to control fins.
source: Interestingly, a single dose of 2DG administered at 0 hpa already showed significant smaller regenerates when compared to control fins (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of regenerated area shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: Administration of 2DG between 0-12, 0-24, and 0-36 hpa had a dose-dependent inhibitory effect on the overall regenerated area.
source: Administration of 2DG between 0–12, 0–24, and 0–36 hpa had a dose-dependent inhibitory effect on the overall regenerated area (Figure 3C and F–K).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of regenerated area shown in Figure 3C and F-K.

claim: Blocking of the glycolytic influx for the first 36 hpa led to a complete abrogation of blastema assembly.
source: Accordingly, blocking of the glycolytic influx for the first 36 hpa led to a complete abrogation of blastema assembly (Figure 3C and J–K).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of regenerated area and images shown in Figure 3C and J-K.

claim: The glycolysis inhibitor 3-(3-pyridinyl)-1-(4-pyridinyl)-2-propen-1-one (3PO) exhibited a general impairment of caudal fin regeneration at 48 hpa in relation to control fins.
source: Similarly, the glycolysis inhibitor acting downstream of 2DG, 3-(3-pyridinyl)–1-(4-pyridinyl)–2-propen-1-one (3PO), which partially inhibits the glycolytic activator of Pfk (Schoors et al., 2014 Figure 3A), also exhibited a general impairment of caudal fin regeneration, as observed at 48 hpa in relation to control fins (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of regenerated area shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D and citation to a previous study (Schoors et al., 2014).

claim: 3PO partially inhibits the glycolytic activator of phosphofructokinase (Pfk).
source: Similarly, the glycolysis inhibitor acting downstream of 2DG, 3-(3-pyridinyl)–1-(4-pyridinyl)–2-propen-1-one (3PO), which partially inhibits the glycolytic activator of Pfk (Schoors et al., 2014 Figure 3A)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Schoors et al., 2014).

claim: Sodium Oxamate (S.O.) administration during the first 36 hpa resulted in a decrease of the caudal fin regenerated area in respect to control caudal fins.
source: S.O. administration during the first 36 hpa resulted in a decrease of the caudal fin regenerated area in respect to control caudal fins (Figure 3L–O), although exhibiting a milder effect when compared to glycolysis inhibition (Figure 3C–K and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of regenerated area shown in Figure 3L-O.

claim: Sodium Oxamate (S.O.) exhibited a milder effect on regeneration when compared to glycolysis inhibition.
source: S.O. administration during the first 36 hpa resulted in a decrease of the caudal fin regenerated area in respect to control caudal fins (Figure 3L–O), although exhibiting a milder effect when compared to glycolysis inhibition (Figure 3C–K and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of quantification data shown in Figure 3L-O and Figure 3C-K.

claim: Inhibition of OXPHOS using a mitochondrial pyruvate carrier inhibitor (UK5099) led to a mild, although significant, increase in the regenerated area at 48 hpa when compared to control fins.
source: In contrast, inhibition of OXPHOS using a mitochondrial pyruvate carrier inhibitor (UK5099) (Hildyard et al., 2005; Figure 3A) led to a mild, although significant, increase in the regenerated area at 48 hpa when compared to control fins (Figure 3P-S), suggesting an improvement of the regenerative ability.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of regenerated area shown in Figure 3P-S and citation to a previous study (Hildyard et al., 2005).

claim: Inhibition of OXPHOS using UK5099 suggests an improvement of the regenerative ability.
source: In contrast, inhibition of OXPHOS using a mitochondrial pyruvate carrier inhibitor (UK5099) (Hildyard et al., 2005; Figure 3A) led to a mild, although significant, increase in the regenerated area at 48 hpa when compared to control fins (Figure 3P-S), suggesting an improvement of the regenerative ability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed increase in regenerated area shown in Figure 3P-S.

claim: The same effect was not observed using an inhibitor of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (MitoBlock-6 (MB6)).
source: The same effect was not observed using an inhibitor of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (MitoBlock-6 (MB6)) (Dabir et al., 2013; Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of regenerated area shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-H and citation to a previous study (Dabir et al., 2013).

claim: Glycolysis and lactate generation, but not OXPHOS, are essential for the initial stages of caudal fin regeneration.
source: Together, these results indicate that glycolysis and lactate generation, but not OXPHOS, are essential for the initial stages of caudal fin regeneration.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the pharmacological manipulation experiments presented in the section.

claim: Cells that respond to amputation reprogram their metabolic profile to stimulate the glycolytic machinery/influx to support blastema formation.
source: Our data strongly supports the hypothesis that the cells that respond to amputation reprogram their metabolic profile since very early thereby stimulating the glycolytic machinery/influx to support blastema formation.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

claim: Inhibition of the glycolytic influx led to a significant upregulation of bglap at 24 hpa.
source: We observed that inhibition of the glycolytic influx led to a significant upregulation of bglap and to a decrease in both runx2 orthologues (Figure 4C)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Inhibition of the glycolytic influx led to a decrease in both runx2 orthologues at 24 hpa.
source: We observed that inhibition of the glycolytic influx led to a significant upregulation of bglap and to a decrease in both runx2 orthologues (Figure 4C)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 2DG treatment had no effect on the number of dedifferentiated Runx2+Bglap+ pre-osteoblasts at 24 hpa.
source: Immunofluorescence analysis for Runx2 in bglap:EGFP reporter fish, showed that 2DG treatment had no effect in the number of dedifferentiated Runx2 +Bglap + pre-OBs (Figure 4D–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 4D-G.

claim: The number of Runx2+Bglap- pre-osteoblasts was significantly reduced upon 2DG treatment at 24 hpa when compared to control fins.
source: However, the number of Runx2 +Bglap- pre-OBs was significantly reduced (Figure 4E–G) when compared to control fins (Figure 4D, F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 4D-G.

claim: Blocking glycolytic influx hampers mature osteoblast dedifferentiation, which become unable to operate as a source of pre-osteoblasts resulting in impaired pre-osteoblast pool assembly within the blastema primordium.
source: Overall, these data indicate that blocking glycolytic influx hampers mature OB dedifferentiation, which become unable to operate as a source of pre-OB resulting in impaired pre-OB pool assembly within the blastema primordium.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

claim: During homeostasis, NF-kB pathway maintains retinoic acid (RA) signalling in osteoblasts, supporting differentiation.
source: During homeostasis NF-kB pathway maintains retinoic acid (RA) signalling in OBs, supporting differentiation.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the NF-kB-RA axis in osteoblast differentiation.

claim: Upon amputation, NF-kB pathway becomes inactivated and RA is degraded through activity of the RA-degrading enzyme, Cyp26b1, thereby inducing osteoblast dedifferentiation.
source: Upon amputation, NF-kB pathway becomes inactivated and RA is degraded through activity of the RA-degrading enzyme, Cyp26b1, thereby inducing OB dedifferentiation (Mishra et al., 2020; Blum and Begemann, 2015; Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Mishra et al., 2020; Blum and Begemann, 2015) and illustrated in Figure 4A.

claim: Bmp signaling is considered to be a potent inducer of osteoblast differentiation during regeneration.
source: In addition, Bmp signaling is also considered to be a potent inducer of OB differentiation during regeneration (Stewart et al., 2014; Brandão et al., 2019; Smith et al., 2006; Quint et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Stewart et al., 2014; Brandão et al., 2019; Smith et al., 2006; Quint et al., 2002).

claim: At 24 hpa, there is an increase in NF-kB target genes (nfkbiaa and nfkbiab) in 2DG-treated fins.
source: We observed an increase in NF-kB target genes and in bmp2b, accompanied by a decrease in cyp26b1 in 2DG-treated fins.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: At 24 hpa, there is an increase in bmp2b in 2DG-treated fins.
source: We observed an increase in NF-kB target genes and in bmp2b, accompanied by a decrease in cyp26b1 in 2DG-treated fins.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: At 24 hpa, there is a decrease in cyp26b1 in 2DG-treated fins.
source: We observed an increase in NF-kB target genes and in bmp2b, accompanied by a decrease in cyp26b1 in 2DG-treated fins.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Suppression of glycolysis seems to maintain the mature osteoblast differentiation profile and to prevent their dedifferentiation after amputation, resembling a pre-amputation scenario.
source: Thus, suppression of glycolysis seems to maintain the mature OB differentiation profile and to prevent their dedifferentiation after amputation, resembling a pre-amputation scenario.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed gene expression changes upon 2DG treatment shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 2DG administration had no effect on the ability of osteoblasts to migrate and reach the amputation zone at 24 hpa.
source: Surprisingly, by measuring the relative cell displacement of the OB population in the first segment below the amputation region after 24 hpa, we observed that 2DG administration had no effect on the ability of OB to migrate and reach the amputation zone (Figure 5A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-imaging quantification data shown in Figure 5A-E.

claim: Cell cycle re-entry was strongly affected by 2DG treatment at 24 hpa.
source: However, cell cycle re-entry, examined through a EdU 3 hr pulse assay in bglap:EGFP transgenics, was strongly affected by 2DG treatment (Figure 5F–G') contrasting with control caudal fins.
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling data shown in Figure 5F-G'.

claim: There is a significant reduction of total number of Runx2+Bglap+EdU+ pre-osteoblasts per area upon 2DG treatment at 24 hpa.
source: We observed a significant reduction of total number of Runx2 +Bglap + EdU +pre OBs per area (Figure 5H) and percentage of Runx2 +Bglap + EdU +within the Runx2 +Bglap + population (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling quantification data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: There is a significant reduction in the percentage of Runx2+Bglap+EdU+ within the Runx2+Bglap+ population upon 2DG treatment at 24 hpa.
source: We observed a significant reduction of total number of Runx2 +Bglap + EdU +pre OBs per area (Figure 5H) and percentage of Runx2 +Bglap + EdU +within the Runx2 +Bglap + population (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling quantification data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: There is a reduction in the number and relative percentage of Runx2+Bglap-EdU+ pre-osteoblasts upon 2DG treatment at 24 hpa.
source: By quantifying the remaining pre-OB population Runx2 +Bglap-, we also observed a reduction in the number and relative percentage of Runx2 +Bglap-EdU+pre OBs upon 2DG treatment (Figure 5F–G' arrows, H,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling quantification data shown in Figure 5F-G', H, I.

claim: Blocking glycolytic machinery has a severe impact on the number of pre-osteoblasts that re-enter the cell cycle, reducing their proliferative capacity.
source: This indicates that blocking glycolytic machinery has a severe impact in the number of pre-OB that re-enter the cell cycle, reducing their proliferative capacity.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the EdU labeling data presented in the section.

claim: Inhibition of cell cycle re-entry by 2DG was also observed in the blastema primordium mesenchyme at 24 hpa.
source: This inhibition of cell cycle re-entry by 2DG was also observed in the blastema primordium mesenchyme (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-F,H) and the overlying epidermal cap (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-F,H.

claim: Inhibition of cell cycle re-entry by 2DG was also observed in the overlying epidermal cap at 24 hpa.
source: This inhibition of cell cycle re-entry by 2DG was also observed in the blastema primordium mesenchyme (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-F,H) and the overlying epidermal cap (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-F,G.

claim: There is a downregulation of wnt10a, igf2b and fgf20a in 2DG-treated caudal fins at 24 hpa in comparison to controls.
source: This is predicted based on our results showing a downregulation of wnt10a, igf2b and fgf20a in 2DG-treated caudal fins in comparison to controls (Figure 5J).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The decline in the capacity of pre-osteoblasts to re-enter the cell cycle and to proliferate could be correlated with defects in the activity of Wnt, Insulin and Fgf signaling pathways.
source: Moreover, the decline in the capacity of pre-OB to re-enter the cell cycle and to proliferate could be correlated with defects in the activity of pathways known to be indispensable for blastema proliferation, such as, Wnt, Insulin and Fgf signaling pathways (Lee et al., 2005; Poss et al., 2000; Stoick-Cooper et al., 2007; Chablais and Jazwinska, 2010; Wehner and Weidinger, 2015; Shibata et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed downregulation of wnt10a, igf2b and fgf20a, combined with citations to previous studies (Lee et al., 2005; Poss et al., 2000; Stoick-Cooper et al., 2007; Chablais and Jazwinska, 2010; Wehner and Weidinger, 2015; Shibata et al., 2016).

claim: Wnt, Insulin and Fgf signaling pathways are indispensable for blastema proliferation.
source: Moreover, the decline in the capacity of pre-OB to re-enter the cell cycle and to proliferate could be correlated with defects in the activity of pathways known to be indispensable for blastema proliferation, such as, Wnt, Insulin and Fgf signaling pathways (Lee et al., 2005; Poss et al., 2000; Stoick-Cooper et al., 2007; Chablais and Jazwinska, 2010; Wehner and Weidinger, 2015; Shibata et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Lee et al., 2005; Poss et al., 2000; Stoick-Cooper et al., 2007; Chablais and Jazwinska, 2010; Wehner and Weidinger, 2015; Shibata et al., 2016).

claim: 3PO led to a reduction in cell cycle re-entry of Bglap+ pre-osteoblasts, mesenchymal and epidermal cells at 24 hpa, measured by PCNA immunofluorescence.
source: We further complement and confirmed our results using 3PO, a partial glycolytic inhibitor, in bglap:EGFP transgenic fish. In accordance with previous results, 3PO led to a reduction in cell cycle re-entry of Bglap +pre OB, mesenchymal and epidermal cells, measured by PCNA immunofluorescence (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I-O).
evidence: The claim is supported by PCNA immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1I-O.

claim: Except for the mesenchyme compartment, the epidermis and Runx2+ pre-osteoblasts showed no major alterations in TUNEL-positive cells upon 2DG treatment at 24 hpa.
source: Except for the mesenchyme compartment, which showed a slight increase in the number of TUNEL-positive cells, the epidermis and Runx2 +pre OBs showed no major alterations upon 2DG treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-L).
evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL assay quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-L.

claim: The mesenchyme compartment showed a slight increase in the number of TUNEL-positive cells upon 2DG treatment at 24 hpa.
source: Except for the mesenchyme compartment, which showed a slight increase in the number of TUNEL-positive cells, the epidermis and Runx2 +pre OBs showed no major alterations upon 2DG treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-L).
evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL assay quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-L.

claim: Glycolysis may support cell survival in the mesenchymal compartment, but not in the epidermis or in the pre-osteoblast pools.
source: This suggests that glycolysis may support cell survival in the mesenchymal compartment, but not in the epidermis or in the pre-OB pools.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the TUNEL assay data showing differential effects of 2DG treatment on different tissue compartments.

claim: Blocking glycolysis is sufficient to inhibit osteoblast dedifferentiation and cell cycle re-entry, without affecting their capacity to migrate or survive.
source: Thus, blocking glycolysis is sufficient to inhibit OB dedifferentiation and cell cycle re-entry, without affecting their capacity to migrate or survive.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

claim: Enhancing glycolysis promotes mature osteoblast dedifferentiation into pre-osteoblasts and enabling pre-osteoblasts and other lineages to re-acquire proliferative capacity within the blastema.
source: Taken together, our results reveal that enhancing glycolysis promotes mature OB dedifferentiation into pre-OB and enabling pre-OB and other lineages to re-acquire proliferative capacity within the blastema.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

claim: Energy metabolism controls osteoblast dedifferentiation and cell cycle re-entry through a glycolysis-dependent transcriptional regulation.
source: We also provide evidence that energy metabolism controls these aspects of OB response to injury through a glycolysis-dependent transcriptional regulation.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

claim: Metabolic reprogramming toward glycolysis is a novel and powerful conductor of the cell fate changes and cell cycle re-entry preceding blastema assembly.
source: Therefore, these results provide solid evidence that metabolic reprogramming toward glycolysis is a novel and powerful conductor of the cell fate changes and cell cycle re-entry preceding blastema assembly.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the section.

claim: At 48 hpa, the blastema is subdivided in a patterning zone (PZ) and in a proximal (PB) and distal (DB) compartments.
source: At 48 hpa, the blastema is subdivided in a patterning zone (PZ) and in a proximal (PB) and distal (DB) compartments.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about blastema organization.

claim: Proliferative Runx2+ pre-osteoblasts maintain the progenitor pool in the proximal blastema (PB).
source: These regions are characterized by distinct OB subtypes, based on their maturation and proliferative state, exhibiting a proximal-distal hierarchical and overlapping distribution (Wehner and Weidinger, 2015; Iovine, 2007; Nechiporuk and Keating, 2002; Poss et al., 2002): proliferative Runx2+ pre-OBs maintain the progenitor pool in the PB
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Wehner and Weidinger, 2015; Iovine, 2007; Nechiporuk and Keating, 2002; Poss et al., 2002).

claim: As pre-osteoblasts proliferate and become further away from the influence of the distal blastema signals, they start to differentiate into proliferative lineage committed Runx2+Osx+ immature osteoblasts.
source: and, as they proliferate and become further away from the influence of the DB signals, they start to differentiate into proliferative lineage committed Runx2+ Osx+ immature OBs (Stewart et al., 2014; Brown et al., 2009)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Stewart et al., 2014; Brown et al., 2009).

claim: Proliferative lineage committed Runx2+Osx+ immature osteoblasts will give rise to differentiated osteoblasts in the patterning zone (PZ).
source: and, as they proliferate and become further away from the influence of the DB signals, they start to differentiate into proliferative lineage committed Runx2+ Osx+ immature OBs (Stewart et al., 2014; Brown et al., 2009), which will give rise to differentiated OBs in the PZ (Figure 6B; Stewart et al., 2014; Brown et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Stewart et al., 2014; Brown et al., 2009) and illustrated in Figure 6B.

claim: Prolonged 2DG-treatment caused a severe abrogation of blastema organization at 48 hpa.
source: We observed that prolonged 2DG-treatment caused a severe abrogation of blastema organization (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-H)
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-H.

claim: Prolonged 2DG-treatment caused a strong reduction in osx expression at 48 hpa when compared to control fins.
source: We observed that prolonged 2DG-treatment caused a severe abrogation of blastema organization (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-H), with a strong reduction in osx (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,F,D,H) and runx2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D,G,H) when compared to control fins
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,F,D,H.

claim: Prolonged 2DG-treatment caused a strong reduction in runx2 expression at 48 hpa when compared to control fins.
source: We observed that prolonged 2DG-treatment caused a severe abrogation of blastema organization (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-H), with a strong reduction in osx (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,F,D,H) and runx2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D,G,H) when compared to control fins
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D,G,H.

claim: 2DG administration strongly alters osteoblast specific gene expression within the blastema at 48 hpa.
source: We observed that prolonged 2DG-treatment caused a severe abrogation of blastema organization (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-H), with a strong reduction in osx (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,F,D,H) and runx2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D,G,H) when compared to control fins, indicating that 2DG administration strongly alters OB specific gene expression within the blastema.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed reduction in osx and runx2 expression shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In normal regenerating conditions, the cluster of Runx2+Osx- pre-osteoblasts is restricted to the proximal blastema (PB) and represents a smaller fraction of the osteoblast lineage in the blastema at 48 hpa.
source: The cluster of Runx2 +pre OBs, referred as the Runx2 +Osx- subtype, is restricted to the PB and represents a smaller fraction of the OB lineage in the blastema (Figure 6C, C' and E)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6C, C' and E.

claim: In normal regenerating conditions, immature osteoblasts (Runx2+Osx+) reside in the interface between the proximal blastema (PB) region and the patterning zone (PZ), and correspond to the major osteoblast subtype at 48 hpa.
source: while immature OBs, referred as the Runx2 +Osx + subtype, reside in the interface between the PB region and the PZ, and correspond to the major OB subtype (Figure 6C, C' and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6C, C' and F.

claim: 2DG-treated fish had an accentuated decrease in the total number of Runx2+Osx+ immature osteoblasts at 48 hpa.
source: In contrast, we observe that 2DG-treated fish had an accentuated decrease in the total number of Runx2+Osx+ immature OBs (Figure 6D, D' and F)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6D, D' and F.

claim: Runx2+Osx- pre-osteoblasts remain unchanged in 2DG-treated fish at 48 hpa.
source: In contrast, we observe that 2DG-treated fish had an accentuated decrease in the total number of Runx2+Osx+ immature OBs (Figure 6D, D' and F), while Runx2+Osx- pre-OBs remain unchanged (Figure 6D, D' and E)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6D, D' and E.

claim: 2DG treatment leads to an imbalance between the osteoblast populations within the blastema at 48 hpa.
source: In contrast, we observe that 2DG-treated fish had an accentuated decrease in the total number of Runx2+Osx+ immature OBs (Figure 6D, D' and F), while Runx2+Osx- pre-OBs remain unchanged (Figure 6D, D' and E), leading to an imbalance between the OB populations within the blastema (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed changes in osteoblast subtype numbers shown in Figure 6D-G.

claim: Similar results were obtained when using the glycolytic inhibitor 3PO at 48 hpa.
source: Similar results were obtained when using the glycolytic inhibitor 3PO (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I-O).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1I-O.

claim: In normal regenerating conditions, Runx2+Osx+ immature osteoblasts exhibit a higher proliferation rate than Runx2+Osx- pre-osteoblasts at 48 hpa.
source: As previously reported (Stewart et al., 2014), in control fins Runx2 +Osx + immature OBs exhibit a higher proliferation rate than Runx2 +Osx- pre-OBs (Figure 6H, H', J and K).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling data shown in Figure 6H, H', J and K and citation to a previous study (Stewart et al., 2014).

claim: Glycolysis inhibition had a more profound impact on proliferation at 48 hpa than at 24 hpa.
source: Strikingly, glycolysis inhibition had a more profound impact on proliferation at 48 hpa (Figure 6I–K) than at 24 hpa (Figure 5F–I)
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of EdU labeling data shown in Figure 6I-K and Figure 5F-I.

claim: Both osteoblast subtypes exhibited a significant reduction of their proliferative capacity upon glycolysis inhibition at 48 hpa.
source: Strikingly, glycolysis inhibition had a more profound impact on proliferation at 48 hpa (Figure 6I–K) than at 24 hpa (Figure 5F–I), with both OB subtypes exhibiting a significant reduction of their proliferative capacity (Figure 6H–K).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling quantification data shown in Figure 6H-K.

claim: The reduction in proliferation upon glycolysis inhibition at 48 hpa was particularly noticeable in Runx2+Osx+ osteoblast subtype.
source: This reduction was particularly noticeable in Runx2 +Osx + OB subtype.
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling quantification data shown in Figure 6H-K.

claim: The epidermis and mesenchyme displayed a decrease in proliferation in 2-DG-treated fish at 48 hpa.
source: We also noticed that, as observed at 24 hpa (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G,H), the epidermis and mesenchyme were also affected, displaying a decrease in proliferation in 2-DG-treated fish (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-H).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-H.

claim: Both pre-osteoblast and immature osteoblast populations accumulate at the stump region since they are unable to proceed in the cell cycle and divide upon 2DG treatment.
source: Given the results obtained, the most likely interpretation is that both pre-OB and immature OB populations accumulate at the stump region since they are unable to proceed in the cell cycle and divide.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed reduction in proliferation and changes in osteoblast distribution upon 2DG treatment.

claim: In normal regenerating conditions, dedifferentiated osteoblasts were found near the stump region, contributing to the blastema at 48 hpa.
source: In fact, corroborating these observations, when monitoring Runx2 +Bglap + pre-OB, using bglap:EGFP line, at 48 hpa, we observed that while in normal regenerating conditions dedifferentiated OBs were found near the stump region, contributing to the blastema (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,A',C) as previously demonstrated (Knopf et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,A',C and citation to a previous study (Knopf et al., 2011).

claim: After 2DG inhibition, dedifferentiated osteoblasts remained accumulated at the stump at 48 hpa, indicative of their inability to progress during the regenerative process.
source: In fact, corroborating these observations, when monitoring Runx2 +Bglap + pre-OB, using bglap:EGFP line, at 48 hpa, we observed that while in normal regenerating conditions dedifferentiated OBs were found near the stump region, contributing to the blastema (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,A',C) as previously demonstrated (Knopf et al., 2011), after 2DG inhibition these cells remained accumulated at the stump, indicative of their inability to progress during the regenerative process (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B,B',C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B,B',C.

claim: The Runx2+Osx+ immature osteoblasts found near the stump region in the 2DG context are, at least in part, still osteoblasts that were unable to fully dedifferentiate after fin amputation.
source: These data let us to further hypothesized that the Runx2 +Osx + immature OBs found near the stump region in the 2DG context (Figure 6D, D', I, I'), are, at least in part, still OBs that were unable to fully dedifferentiate after fin amputation.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis inferred from the observed distribution of osteoblast subtypes upon 2DG treatment shown in Figure 6D, D', I, I'.

claim: After 2DG administration, Runx2+Osx- pre-osteoblasts are still able to be recruited at 48 hpa, but do not increase in total numbers due to inability to proliferate.
source: Also, it is noteworthy mentioning that after 2DG administration, Runx2 +Osx- pre-OBs are still able to be recruited at this stage, but do not increase in total numbers due to inability to proliferate.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed numbers of Runx2+Osx- pre-osteoblasts and their proliferation rates upon 2DG treatment.

claim: Although osteoblast dedifferentiation is compromised after blocking the glycolytic influx, pre-osteoblasts may be generated by alternative sources.
source: Interestingly, this may indicate that, although OB dedifferentiation is compromised after blocking the glycolytic influx, pre-OB may be generated by alternative sources.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the observation that Runx2+Osx- pre-osteoblasts are still present after 2DG treatment.

claim: While control fish are able to efficiently reconstruct the lost skeletal tissue at 7 days post-amputation (dpa), in 2DG-treated animals bone regeneration was completely abolished.
source: By extending 2DG treatment into the outgrowth and patterning phase of regeneration (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A), we observe that while control fish are able to efficiently reconstruct the lost skeletal tissue at 7 days post-amputation (dpa) (Figure 6—figure supplement 4C,D), in 2DG-treated animals bone regeneration was completely abolished (Figure 6—figure supplement 4E, F).
